title: A reusable scripted playtest harness for the probe app
goal: Three audits in a row have each rebuilt a throwaway harness to drive the real editor with scripted clicks and keys and render the window offscreen. Keep one in the repo, switched on only by a request file, so the next audit starts from a working walk instead of from nothing.
notes: Reusable harness: script model PhotonzCore/PlaytestScript.swift (PlaytestScriptTests), driver Sources/Photonz/Playtest/PlaytestHarness.swift under #if PHOTONZ_PLAYTEST (defined by build-app.sh for dev+probe variants, not release) and gated at runtime on AppInfo.flavor == .probe. Hooks: AppDelegate.applicationDidFinishLaunching -> PlaytestHarness.startIfRequested; EditorState.canvasDidMoveToWindow -> PlaytestHarness.register. Launch: Scripts/playtest.sh <script.json> (wraps probe-app.sh --playtest, waits for done.json, quits the probe). Example: Scripts/playtest/redline-walk.json. Doc: docs/design/playtest-harness.md. The old throwaway (temp/redline-walk) is superseded. Capture overlay + toast are not scripted; menu shortcuts that use @FocusedValue no-op in the inactive probe (use the action step).
acceptance: A file-triggered harness in the app drives the probe editor with synthesized events and writes renders plus a JSON log, off by default and never reachable in the shipping build
A short doc says how to run it
Scripts/test.sh green; the dev and shipping bundles behave exactly as before

log.note: epic measure-redline -> unmanned-loop, area app -> queue (triage 2026-09-02): loop tooling that serves the focus by making every audit start from a working walk
Epic unmanned-loop is staged next, not now, but triage on 2026-09-02 kept this task open because it serves the focus (measure-redline audits are how that feature reaches the user). Doing it.

Review before building: the old harness hardcoded the whole walk in Swift, so every audit had to edit and recompile. The reusable shape is a JSON script the probe interprets (open, key, move, click, drag, type, snapshot, describe, clipboard) so a new walk is a new file, not new code. The capture-overlay stage is left out: it needs private selection types opened up and a synthetic desktop, and it is the piece most likely to rot; noted as a rough edge. Compile gate: a PHOTONZ_PLAYTEST define set by build-app.sh for the dev and probe variants only (they share one compiled product, so no rebuild churn between them); runtime gate on the probe bundle id, so the dev app never runs it and the shipping build never contains it.

Built: PlaytestScript (PhotonzCore, 8 tests) + PlaytestHarness (app, #if PHOTONZ_PLAYTEST, probe flavor only) + Scripts/playtest.sh, probe-app.sh --playtest, build-app.sh define for non-release variants, docs/design/playtest-harness.md, example Scripts/playtest/redline-walk.json.

Verified: the example walk runs 69 steps in ~13s with status ok and 15 renders; Scripts/test.sh green (1296 tests); a release-configuration build without the define carries no harness strings while the probe bundle does; dev app untouched (never built, never killed).

Review after building: chords through NSApp were dropped (inactive app has no key window), now offered to the window then the menu bar and the log says who took them; menu items acting on the focused editor still no-op because the probe is never active, so the action step covers copy outcomes. The walk found two product warts, queued: Size mode calipers named Gap, and the midpoint handle covering the readout.

Shipped: PlaytestScript (PhotonzCore, tested) + PlaytestHarness (app, PHOTONZ_PLAYTEST + probe-only) + Scripts/playtest.sh + example Scripts/playtest/redline-walk.json + docs/design/playtest-harness.md. Verified: the walk runs 69 steps with status ok and 15 renders; Scripts/test.sh green (1296 tests); release build carries no harness strings; dev app never touched.
